title: Special Forces Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-180A. Military Occupational Specialty 180A--Special Forces Warrant Officer
   a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 6016.
   c. MOS 180A. MOS 180A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are 18B, 18C,
18D, 18E, 18F and 18Z.
   d. Associated SQI.
       (1) 0--No special qualifications.
       (2) 8--Instructor.
       (3) T--Transition (personnel only).
       (4) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
       (1) 4W--Underwater Special Operations.
       (2) 4X--Military Free Fall Special Forces.
       (3) D5 – Regional Support Element (Effective 202410)
       (4) J4 –Jedburgh Operator.
   f. Qualifications.
       (1) WO1/CW2 must—
             (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
             (b) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to sensitive
compartmental information (SCI).
             (c) Complete the Special Forces Warrant Officers Technical and Tactical Certification
Course.
             (d) Be able to perform parachute duty.
             (e) Be able to pass the Special Forces swim test.
             (f) Possess a language rating of 2/2 reflected on a current DA Form 330.
             (g) Meet the Medical Fitness Standards for Special Forces duty per AR 40-501,
Survival, Evasion, Resistance, Escape (SERE) training and free fall parachute duty and/or marine
diving duty.

        (2) CW3 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
             (b) Complete the Special Forces Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
        (3) CW4 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
             (b) Complete the Warrant Officers Staff Course (WOSC).
        (4) CW5 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
             (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
    g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
             (a) Command an Operational Detachment Alpha(ODA).
             (b) Commands a task organized operational element as needed.
             (c) Commands half the ODA during split team operations.
             (d) Provides advise in the areas of Special Forces operational administration,
intelligence, operations, logistics, civil-military affairs, and psychological operations.
             (e) Develops, maintains, and continually updates operational plans and targeting data
for deployable elements.
             (f) Assists in the management of predeployment planning, training, and development
of operational detachments.
             (g) Develops, directs, supervises, and conducts training for U.S. and foreign
military/paramilitary forces.
             (h) Provides advice on all aspects of Special Forces operations and specialized
training to include: Military Free Fall (MFF), Combat Dive, Special Operations Training (SOT),
Survival Evasion Resistance Escape (SERE), Special Forces Target Interdiction (SOTI), Special
Forces Advanced Reconnaissance Target Analysis and Exploitation (SFARTAEC), Advanced
 Special Operations Techniques (ASOT), Psychological Operations (PSYOP), and Civil Affairs
(CA).
             (i) Provides advise on the regional considerations of Special Forces operations in the
operational environment based upon cultural awareness, regional ability and linguistic skills.
        (2) CW3--
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
             (b) Advises the Operational Detachment Bravo (ODB) commander on all matters
pertaining to warrant officer assignments, professional development and accessions.
        (3) CW4
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(b) and (d-i).
             (b) Advises the Battalion Commander on all matters pertaining to warrant officer
assignments, professional development, and accessions.
        (4) CW5--
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(b) and (d-i).
             (b) Advises the Group Commander on all matters pertaining to warrant officer
assignments, professional development, and accessions.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Heavy (Black).
        (2) Table 8-180A-1. Physical requirements.
        (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-180A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (b) Table 8-180A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
